fixes.explanation: David doesn't mention giving the kings any commands in these verses. He says they will sing "…for the glory of the LORD is great." The reason he gives is the LORD's glory, not anything David says.

Nothing in David's final lines asks for his own name to be made great. The name that gets lifted up is God's, since David says God has lifted His name and His word above all else (Psalm 138:2). His closing request is, "…do not abandon the works of Your hands."
